articles.title: Man City vs Liverpool: Why graduating from WSL winner to champion is so important to Alex Greenwood
articles.summary: In conversation with Sky Sports before the start of the season, Man City captain Alex Greenwood explains her desire to lead a team of champions - not just winners; watch Man City vs Liverpool live on Sky Sports+ on Friday; kick-off 7pm
articles.body:
Beginning the new campaign with back-to-back victories - the only team to do so - is testament to Greenwood's belief that there is a clear distinction between being a winner and being a champion. Becoming a champion is a process, one that can only be complete by consistently backing up what has already been achieved.

Only one side has maximum points after the first two match rounds of this term, something that has not happened since 2015. Already, the WSL holders appear to be the ones to beat, picking up their baton and attacking the first leg of the race like consummate professionals. They have left the red half of Manchester for dust.

Greenwood herself has been a pillar of consistency under Andree Jeglertz. The beauty of this Manchester City team, actually, is how the sum of all its parts makes such a complete whole, bound together by one guiding rule: "We always find a way".

In conversation at Man City's training base, before a ball was kicked, the 32-year-old explains that her approach to this season will be framed differently. Because you are title holders, I surmise, rather presumptuously? Not the case.

"I needed a mental switch off," she replies, "this summer I had freedom, no schedule, and that is why I feel so fresh now. I can't remember the last time I got that long off, so I definitely enjoyed it."

Plenty changed for Greenwood over her summer of rest, not least getting engaged to long-term partner Jack, despite trying to bail on the plans they had on the evening of the proposal, not knowing what was about to happen.

"If I'm being really honest, the day of, I tried to cancel plans," she continues, smiling at the thought of it. "I wasn't in the mood to go out. But Jack told me he'd paid a heavy deposit on the restaurant. He played it very cool, didn't give much away, and it was amazing."

Beyond that, Greenwood describes this summer as a "necessary reset". The responsibility she carries as a captain means she constantly has "tabs open", unable to completely switch off from the demands of her own high standards as well as the team's. Like a never-ending homework assignment.

"I'm not the kind of person to turn it all off, I'm on the majority of the time. I reflect a lot. I needed a break, because a captain has a huge role off the pitch. But I'm lucky with the dressing room we have, we're very close, it's an open environment to speak. I'm not the only one with the authority to make big calls."

Ruminating on last season should conjure fond memories. City were the dominant force, WSL leaders from early November and worthy winners of their first title in a decade. The football was freer, more inventive - guided by Jeglertz's philosophy rather than burdened by it.

Reinvention happened all over the pitch, from player to player, game to game. Opponents braced before playing City, not knowing what to expect or how to predict their ever-evolving patterns of play. Even when they were unremarkable, they almost always got the job done.

"I get asked a lot about pressure, and certain results made for pressure moments last season. We don't enjoy to lose. But in reality, we were in control. That helps with your preparation, with everything really. We had setbacks but we also had a safety net. That is what we do, always find a way."

City have edge now, a brand of nastiness that felt absent in previous title chases despite getting close. They did not need complete overhaul. "The manager made subtle differences with big results," Greenwood says. Jeglertz describes the adjustment as "never being satisfied", an unappeasable need to improve to a painstaking level of detail.

"He's very open to challenge," Greenwood adds. "He invites it. He wants us to challenge him and each other. It's such a competitive league. Teams have strengthened so much this summer, I love it. We remind each other we are winners, that fuels us to want to remain that. But we have huge respect for the level of opposition we face."

Man City have momentum on their side. They have developed multiple solutions for most problems. Gone are the days where their mental toughness is questioned after one stray result. The complication now is to maintain standards across every competition while also playing in Europe.

"I live for European nights," Greenwood says, touching on her frustration at having to watch last season's Champions League play out from her living room. "Do you know how hard it is to watch those games and not be involved?"

These are questions with implications that extend well beyond pre-season. How will City cope with the increased demands? Can they adapt to the relentless rhythm of three games a week? And does the squad possess enough depth and quality to compete on every front?

"We weren't there last year and we have to use that feeling to our advantage. "We cannot waste our opportunity."

City spent a decade trying to unlock the secret to becoming a WSL winner. The team has been furnished with everything it needs to stay that way: A new £10m training facility, an inspirational manager with aspirational targets, an influx of WSL-ready talent. A superb captain. And of course they have Bunny Shaw; the PFA player of the year is already off to a flyer.

In a Women's Super League season where consistency has already hampered their biggest rivals, City's will to win appears more resolute than ever. They do not intend to be a one hit wonder. They have worked too hard to just be considered winners. They want to qualify as champions.

articles.title: Ibai Gómez y el optimismo por bandera: "Hay tantas cosas positivas que debemos disfrutarlas"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Real Zaragoza, que ha encadenado dos triunfos seguidos, está encantado con el equipo y disfrutando del proceso
articles.summary: El técnico del Real Zaragoza, que ha encadenado dos triunfos seguidos, está encantado con el equipo y disfrutando del proceso
articles.body: Ibai Gómez es un hombre feliz. Los dos últimos triunfos todavía han reforzado esa visión optimista y alegre que tiene como entrenador: "Hay tantas cosas positivas que debemos disfrutarlas. De ilusión y energía me vais a ver así hasta el último día que esté aquí, ojalá sea dentro de mucho tiempo. Quiero disfrutar del proceso y del día a día. Estamos empezando a ilusionar a la gente que era nuestro primer objetivo. Queremos hacer un gran partido el domingo". El vasco reconoce que ganando superará en puntos el primer bloque de cuatro partidos. Y es que, su objetivo es sacar, al menos, siete puntos en estos bloques para pelear por el ascenso directo: "Con un empate entraríamos en ese primer bloque y con una victoria estaríamos uno o dos puntos por encima de los puntos que nos habíamos propuesto". Sobre el estilo de juego, Ibai mantiene que su idea es la que se vio ante el Nástic pese a la derrota: "Hay una forma que nos acerca a ganar y es la del día de Tarragona. A medio y largo plazo eso te hace ganar más. En Torremolinos hicimos un plan diferente y el equipo supo adaptarse. Estoy muy contento con el equipo". Por eso, contra el Cartagena habrá variaciones: "Habrá cambios y cambios de sistema. Van a jugar Jardí y 10 más". Como nombres propios, el entrenador habló sobre Hugo Pinilla, quien no ha participado todavía: "Me fastidia porque es un chaval excepcional y tiene condiciones para aportar, pero he pensado en otro tipo de perfiles que nos acerca a ganar. Tiene que seguir así como está trabajando".

articles.title: Julián, el mejor escenario: todo lo que está haciendo para llegar al derbi
articles.standfirst: El argentino acelera para no perderse el choque del Madrid
articles.summary: El argentino acelera para no perderse el choque del Madrid
articles.body: Julián Alvarez lleva tiempo con un perfil bajo, sin hacer declaraciones, pensando solo en trabajar para alcanzar su mejor nivel. El argentino tenía marcado el derbi en el calendario como el mejor escenario posible para hablar sobre el terreno de juego. Nadie olvida su espectacular actuación en el derbi de la pasada campaña. Y él tampoco. Ese golazo de falta, ese doblete que derrumbó al Real Madrid. Por eso estaba convencido de que el mejor momento para manifestarse sobre el césped era repetir una actuación tan memorable como aquella. De ahí que la lesión sufrida en Anfield fuera un duro golpe para el delantero rojiblanco. Sin embargo, Julián no se ha rendido ante ese frenazo inesperado y lo está dando todo para poder llegar al derbi. El internacional argentino dio síntomas de estar muy recuperado en Liverpool, siendo el mejor rojiblanco sobre el terreno de juego. Sin embargo, unas molestias hicieron saltar la voz de alarma en el vestuario rojiblanco tras el partido de Champions y posteriormente una resonancia magnética confirmó la lesión. Aunque Julián quería estar de vuelta con el equipo el pasado miércoles ante Osasuna y realizó varias sesiones de trabajo en el gimnasio, sobre el césped y con los fisios con ese objetivo, finalmente los servicios médicos aconsejaron prudencia y descartaron su presencia en el encuentro. El gran objetivo de Julián desde que sufriera esa lesión en Anfield ha sido disputar el derbi del próximo domingo. Por eso siguió trabajando en el día de descanso concedido a la plantilla ayer jueves y este viernes comenzó la sesión en solitario sobre el césped media hora antes de incorporarse al grupo para realizar el entrenamiento planificado por el cuerpo técnico. Parece claro que está descartado que pueda disputar todo el partido, pero Julián va a apurar todos los tiempos para entrar en la convocatoria y si fuera necesario, participar en la última fase del partido. No quiere perder la oportunidad de hablar en el césped del Metropolitano demostrando su compromiso y su implicación ante el eterno rival, el mejor escenario posible.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappé cambia Nike por On junto a Thierry Henry
articles.standfirst: La marca suiza entra en el mundo del fútbol de la mano de la estrella del Real Madrid
articles.summary: La marca suiza entra en el mundo del fútbol de la mano de la estrella del Real Madrid
articles.body: El futbolista del Real Madrid Kylian Mbappé ficha por la marca suiza de equipamiento deportivo On, de la que también será embajador global, en sustitución de la multinacional Nike como proveedor técnico, según informó en sus redes sociales. "Sigo soñando con jugar al fútbol. Puede sorprender, viniendo de alguien cuyo trabajo es jugar. Pero es verdad. Sigo soñando jugar con mis amigos, hasta el anochecer, hasta la cena, sólo porque era un juego, antes de que se pudiera convertir en profesión. He perseguido este sueño desde siempre, y me ha llevado a uno de los mayores cambios en mi vida. Ahora estoy rodeado de innovadores que sueñan lo mismo que yo", comienza el texto que acompaña a la publicación. "Llevar el pie tan cerca como sea posible a la pelota. Llevar a la gente tan cerca como sea posible al deporte. Llevar al mundo tan cerca como sea posible al juego. Supongo que así son los sueños que se niegan a cambiar. Suelen ser los que lo cambian todo", termina. Mbappé ha trabajado con Nike como proveedor técnico desde que era un niño, en las categorías inferiores. Su contrato expiró este 2026 y, en lugar de renovarlo, apuesta por una empresa más joven y en la que tendrá más protagonismo en la toma de decisiones. "Lo que me atrajo a On fue la oportunidad de construir algo enteramente nuevo juntos que dé forma al juego del mañana. Quiero aportar mi experiencia y perspectiva a lo que creemos, impulsar lo que se considera posible a través de la innovación, y mantenerme fiel a la alegría del fútbol. Tenemos un sueño compartido, y esto es solo el principio", sentenció el francés, según declaraciones recogidas por On. En la incorporación de Mbappé a On también influyó el hecho de que el francés Thierry Henry es su director de fútbol, cargo en el que lleva trabajando en secreto desde finales de 2025. "Jugará un rol central en el desarrollo estratégico de On Football, desde las relaciones entre producto y atletas hasta cómo On afronta la cultura y el futuro del deporte", afirma la marca. Según la compañía, Mbappé estará "en el corazón de la trayectoria de On en el fútbol", y "aportará su lectura del juego, forjada en el más alto nivel y respaldada por estadísticas extraordinarias", para "trabajar directamente con los equipos de producto de On, integrando su perspectiva de élite en el desarrollo y prueba del calzado y el equipamiento de fútbol futuro". La empresa, fundada en los Alpes suizos en 2010, nació con la idea de revolucionar las zapatillas de correr. El movimiento con Mbappé es su primer contacto con el mundo del fútbol, al que pretenden aplicar su tecnología LightSpray para crear "unas botas ultraprecisas para mujer y para hombre que se adapten al pie como una segunda piel". On busca, en sus palabras, "trabajar de cerca con una selección muy exclusiva de jugadores de élite para repensar el producto según las demandas del juego al mismo tiempo que se aporta una nueva energía a la cultura que lo rodea - que el deporte es más bonito cuando te centras en la simple alegría de jugar, aumentada por la innovación en el producto y las conexiones significativas con comunidades en todo el mundo".

articles.title: Celades se enfrenta a su prueba más delicada
articles.standfirst: El Cádiz recibe al Girona tras sumar solo 3 puntos de 15 posibles y con dudas
articles.summary: El Cádiz recibe al Girona tras sumar solo 3 puntos de 15 posibles y con dudas
articles.body: El Cádiz recibe este sábado al Girona en el Nuevo Mirandilla en un partido con mucho más en juego que los tres puntos. El conjunto catalán, que hace apenas dos temporadas competía en la Champions League, llega a la capital gaditana con una de las plantillas más potentes de Segunda División y con el ascenso como principal objetivo. Para Albert Celades, el encuentro representa una oportunidad para comenzar a disipar las dudas surgidas durante las primeras jornadas, pero también podría suponer un golpe casi mortal a su continuidad en el banquillo amarillo. El técnico aterrizó en Cádiz cuando apenas faltaban cuatro días para el comienzo de la competición. Desde entonces, ha tenido que conocer y ordenar sobre la marcha una plantilla profundamente renovada. El poco margen de preparación ayuda a explicar parte de un comienzo decepcionante, aunque no evita que aumente la inquietud después de sumar únicamente tres puntos de los primeros quince posibles. La situación de Celades no depende exclusivamente de la clasificación. Dentro del club preocupa especialmente la imagen ofrecida por el equipo, que todavía no ha conseguido mostrar una evolución clara ni establecer una identidad reconocible. En el Cádiz consideran que la plantilla posee calidad y alternativas suficientes para comenzar a reflejar una tendencia positiva. Sin embargo, el entrenador ha introducido numerosos cambios tácticos y modificaciones importantes entre jornadas, una circunstancia que ha impedido consolidar las pocas certezas encontradas durante este inicio de campeonato. El debate sobre el banquillo ha ganado presencia durante los últimos días. Una derrota frente al Girona no implicaría automáticamente la destitución de Celades, pero otro encuentro con malas sensaciones podría acelerar la reflexión de la dirección deportiva y abrir la puerta a un relevo. En Cádiz también existe la percepción de que sería precipitado responsabilizar por completo a Celades. El entrenador apenas lleva un mes en la entidad, asumió el cargo con la temporada a punto de comenzar y todavía trabaja en la adaptación de una plantilla prácticamente nueva. Una decisión inmediata chocaría, además, con la paciencia solicitada desde el club para construir este nuevo proyecto. Aun así, el fútbol reduce los plazos cuando no aparecen los resultados ni una mejoría sobre el terreno de juego. Celades no afronta oficialmente una final, pero el partido ante el Girona sí puede marcar su futuro inmediato. Una victoria reforzaría su posición y concedería tranquilidad al equipo; una derrota acompañada de otra mala imagen elevaría todavía más la presión sobre el banquillo del Nuevo Mirandilla.

articles.title: Raphinha: "Pienso renovar con el Barça y ojalá acabe mi carrera aquí"
articles.standfirst: El atacante brasileño se muestra contundente con sus planes de futuro
articles.summary: El atacante brasileño se muestra contundente con sus planes de futuro
articles.body: Raphinha tiene muy claro, clarísimo, su futuro. El delantero brasileño renovó en mayo del año pasado con el Barcelona hasta junio de 2028, pero la entidad catalana y el internacional ya han iniciado nuevos contactos para ampliar más el vínculo. El atacante, de 29 años, firmará la continuidad. Es feliz en el Barça de Flick y en el Spotify Camp Nou. “Sí, pienso renovar. Cuando renové mi contrato, lo hice hasta 2028 con la idea de que tendría 30 o 31 años y no sabía como llegaría, pero, tal como he empezado la temporada, me da para unos años más y estaría muy contento de poder alargar mi contrato", comentó este viernes a RAC 1. "Y Ojalá acabar mi carrera aquí, sin tener que ir a otro sitio”, añadió Raphinha. El internacional es feliz en el Barcelona, donde es una pieza fundamental. Es titular indiscutible, ha jugado todos los partidos y en los siete ha salido de titular, y es el máximo goleador del equipo y de LaLiga. Flick apostó por él de falso 9 y su rendimiento es excelso. El exprofesional del Leeds lidera el Pichichi con nueve tantos, dos más que Lamine Yamal y Kylian Mbappé. En la Champions League, además, festejó dos dianas más. Precisamente, el preparador le elogió este mediodía en la rueda de prensa previa al cruce en el Pizjuán. "En las dos últimas temporadas, empezábamos la presión con el 9 y Raphinha tiene ese hambre y mentalidad. Está a un nivel muy alto. No sólo mete goles, también defiende. Empieza bien la presión. Como capitán, va por delante y los demás le siguen", dijo Flick. Deco también se refirió al internacional brasileño hace unos días y se mostró satisfecho con su rendimiento y con las negociaciones para su ampliación: "Es feliz aquí y eso es importante. El míster le ha sacado el máximo rendimiento con su gestión emocional. Le veo muy bien. Estamos siempre atentos a nuestros jugadores para que no nos pillen por sorpresas las renovaciones... y después tenemos la meritocracia, que haya equilibrios de contratos y que no haya problemas".

articles.title: Manchester United: Michael Carrick refuses to consider job fears
articles.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says there is no point wasting any time worrying if his job is under threat.
articles.body:
Manchester United boss Michael Carrick says it would be "ridiculous" to start thinking how long he has left in the job after "two or three" bad results.

His side visit Fulham on Sunday after an awful week.

After United lost at home to a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men after 23 minutes, Brighton became the first side to come from two goals down to win at Old Trafford in 50 years in their Carabao Cup tie.

United supporters responded to the midweek setback with boos and by chanting against their team.

Carrick said in the aftermath he was "not bothered" by the pressure - a sentiment he reinforced as he spoke to the media before the Fulham trip.

"I know the club, I know the role, I know what's expected here in terms of playing to a certain standard and achieving certain things on the pitch," he added.

"In terms of future and ownership and how long I've got in the job, that's totally not in my thinking. It's ridiculous to think that way in the position I'm in, that's just not on the radar.

"It's two or three games. It's two or three games too many because I really hate losing, but that doesn't mean the world caves in. In some minds it does, it can't for us."

There has been no sense from senior figures inside United that Carrick's position is under threat. They are more focused on the perceived under performance of so many players given the 12 games out of 17 that were won under the 45-year-old over the second half of last season.

By contrast, they have two victories from six games so far, against newly promoted Ipswich - when they had to come from behind - and Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK in the Champions League.

"It's not a catastrophe or a disaster," said Carrick. "It's not the end of the world."

Yet it is the measure of the noise around a club of United's size that is often feels that way.

Carrick accepted issues at Old Trafford are frequently amplified, so they look to be bigger than they actually are.

Despite this, he loves his job - and the club he served with such distinction as a player, and began his coaching career.

"There's great feelings, and there's obviously disappointments, and sometimes the smaller disappointments lead to being a little bit bigger," he added. "It's just part of coping and being at this great football club.

"I wouldn't want to be anywhere else, genuinely.

"It's the best place for me to be, in part because of the times when it's maybe not going to plan. Sometimes they are best times to work your way through, to find out a few things and come out an awful lot stronger."

Externally, the inquests have tended to focus around recruitment - or lack of it, specifically at left-back - United's finances and debt levels, Carrick's relative inexperience and, other than assistant boss Steve Holland, that of his coaches.

"It's not a blame game," said Carrick, who revealed Luke Shaw and new signing Carlos Baleba "have a chance" of being fit for the Craven Cottage meeting.

"We all search for things to look at and point at, or whatever reason it may be and find a blame. Blame me. No problem. I will take the responsibility.

"But it's not about blaming people. It's about us, it's about us finding solutions and being better. That's as a whole football club."

articles.title: LaLiga denuncia insultos contra el Madrid, Osasuna, Sevilla y Ortiz Arias en la jornada 6
articles.standfirst: El organismo traslada a Antiviolencia y a la RFEF los cánticos ofensivos registrados en los estadios del Atlético, Barcelona, Betis y Málaga, que se exponen a multas y cierres parciales
articles.summary: El organismo traslada a Antiviolencia y a la RFEF los cánticos ofensivos registrados en los estadios del Atlético, Barcelona, Betis y Málaga, que se exponen a multas y cierres parciales
articles.body: LaLiga ha remitido un nuevo escrito de denuncia al Comité de Competición de la RFEF y a la Comisión Antiviolencia detallando los cánticos de carácter ofensivo, intolerante e incitadores a la violencia registrados en cuatro encuentros de la sexta jornada del campeonato. Atlético de Madrid – CA Osasuna (16 de septiembre, Riyadh Air Metropolitano) Minutos 29 y 64: Aficionados de la grada de animación (Fondo Sur, sectores 127 a 133) entonaron durante 10 segundos: “Todos a una, puta Osasuna”. Minutos 65 y 84: Desde el mismo sector se profirió el cántico: “Madridistas hijos de puta”. Minuto 68: Se entonó en la misma zona: “Salta pequeño Canguro y a los Madridistas que les den por el culo”. FC Barcelona – Real Racing Club (16 de septiembre, Spotify Camp Nou) Minuto 70: Aficionados locales de la "Grada Gol 1957" (Gol Sud, sectores 20 al 24) entonaron de forma coordinada durante 20 segundos: “Puta Real Madrid, puta Real Madrid”. Real Betis Balompié – Getafe CF (17 de septiembre, Estadio La Cartuja) Minutos -1 y 45+2: Grupo de aficionados en Gol Sur Tribuna Baja entonó: “¡Soria, cabrón, puta de Nervión!”. Minuto 55: En la misma zona se cantó: “¡La Giralda de nuestra ciudad, verá solo un equipo llorar, el equipo bastardo y penoso, el equipo de las putas del Pizjuán!”. Minuto 60: Cántico continuado durante 2 minutos desde el mismo sector: “¡Al fin van a decir la verdad de esos putos bastardos, que la hinchada más triste de todas es la del Sánchez Pizjuán!”. Málaga CF – Villarreal CF (17 de septiembre, La Rosaleda) Minuto 70: Aficionados de la grada Fondo Sur (sectores 112 al 230) dirigieron al colegiado durante 9 segundos el cántico: “¡Árbitro valiente, valiente hijo de puta!”. Los hechos han sido tipificados como comportamientos prohibidos según el Código de Disciplina Deportiva de la RFEF y la Ley contra la violencia, el racismo, la xenofobia y la intolerancia en el deporte. Los clubes denunciados se exponen a resoluciones sancionadoras por parte del Comité de Competición y de Antiviolencia, las cuales pueden abarcar desde multas económicas hasta el cierre parcial de los sectores del estadio donde se originaron de forma focalizada los insultos (Fondo Sur en el Riyadh Air Metropolitano y La Rosaleda; Gol Sud en el Spotify Camp Nou; y Gol Sur Tribuna Baja en La Cartuja).

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel: England boss on 'embracing the chaos' ahead of Nations League fixtures
articles.summary: After the World Cup, England boss Thomas Tuchel wanted greater control. Two months on, he is keen to "embrace the chaos" after naming his squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures.
articles.body:
England manager Thomas Tuchel left the United States in July pining for greater control.

At his first squad announcement since the World Cup on Friday, the German spoke of "embracing the chaos".

Is it possible to have controlled chaos? It seems Tuchel is ready to find out.

England's third-placed finish in the US was the nation's best performance at the World Cup since 1966.

But the memories of the team's semi-final loss to Argentina linger.

In the aftermath of the heartbreaking defeat, Tuchel pointed to his team's inability to find control having taken the lead via Anthony Gordon's opener as a key factor behind his side's late collapse.

Fast-forward two months, however, and the messaging is rather different ahead of the four upcoming Nations League games.

"Football is about adapting to situations and football without any control is sometimes hard to digest for a coach, if you look at the 6-4 against France [in the World Cup bronze-medal match]," said Tuchel.

"But people talk about it like it's one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match, so maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best."

Tuchel recalls Alexander-Arnold and Palmer with warning

Mixed signals? Or maybe it is just a sign that Tuchel wants his side to become more unpredictable in their search for success.

Because that is what the best teams do - mix it up when required.

Despite Tuchel's remarks, his latest squad for the fixtures against Spain, the Czech Republic and Croatia rather contradicts any thoughts of a havoc-rich approach.

The return of Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer, two of English football's most technically gifted players, screams control.

So do the call-ups of Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall, who are both extremely adept in possession of the ball.

Of course, there is certainly a balance to be struck. That would be Tuchel's ideal scenario.

Rio Ngumoha's first senior call-up will certainly add an air of unpredictability to Tuchel's options.

The Liverpool winger, 18, has had an exciting start to the season, catching the eye with his invention and trickery down both flanks for Andoni Iraola's side.

That Tuchel revealed Fulham attacker Josh King is also close to earning his first senior call-up provides further indication the England manager wants to reinvigorate his forward line ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign and beyond.

Yet, we shouldn't expect Tuchel to completely let go of the handbrake just yet.

In response to a question as to whether his team can replicate the fast-paced approach of a Premier League team but harnessed with a greater control, Tuchel responded: "That would be the wish, that we become for 10 minutes a little bit more like Spain, here and there.

"The more I reflect on it, it's maybe more buying into our strengths and play more minutes like we played the second half against Croatia, and more minutes like we played the first half against France, and buying into these strengths, because I think we get a lot of value out of it, we get a lot of connection to the fans, this is what the Premier League reflects.

"We are maybe not the most economical team to play football but this is maybe also a characteristic of the Premier League. The Premier League is not a very economical league, you have to play.

"You need to max out every single match otherwise you cannot compete for the title so this is something more beautiful. But this is where we are, where I am in my mindset and I think where the players are, so it's still a bit ambiguous."

But while Tuchel may not have total clarity with regards to whether control or chaos is the way forward, he showed no hint of confusion over who he believes his best players are.

Tuchel refuted assertions his decision to recall Palmer and Alexander-Arnold was an admission he'd got his World Cup squad wrong.

Indeed, Tuchel has hinted he would have picked a vastly similar squad for the upcoming games to the one he selected for the US had all his options been available.

"Before we did the nomination in the last month, I thought we had more of a continuation of the World Cup squad but then a lot of members of our World Cup squad - Reece [James], Dan [Burn], Dean [Henderson, [John] Stones, [Jordan] Henderson, Djed Spence - can't be with us due to injuries, so it is not like a full continuation.

"These players were crucial for us in building the brotherhood, in building the spirit and taking care of the mentality that took us the long way in the tournament. We will not negotiate on that, we will not give in on that.

"So other players will step up, this is basically how I see this camp.

"My mindset at the moment is not to change too much within the formations."

England host World Cup winners Spain at Wembley on Saturday, 26 September then travel to the Czech Republic (Tuesday, 29 September) and Croatia (Saturday, 3 October) before the Czechs visit on Tuesday, 6 October.

articles.title: El Madrid más ofensivo... pero el más fallón
articles.standfirst: Es el segundo equipo que más dispara a puerta en Europa, solo por detrás del Barça, pero está a la cola en efectividad
articles.summary: Es el equipo que más dispara a puerta pero está a la cola en efectividad entre las grandes ligas
articles.body: Sobre el Real Madrid de Mourinho cuelga el cartel muchas veces de equipo defensivo y de poco vistoso, pero los datos demuestran que hay muchos caminos para llegar al gol al margen del que emplea el Barcelona, que hasta ahora es para casi todos el grupo más en forma del campeonato. Echando un vistazo rápido a las estadísticas, lo cierto es que el equipo blanco disparara y genera más peligro que el azulgrana. No es, por tanto, un problema de juego. Su problema es otro: le cuesta transformar la mayor parte de sus ocasiones en gol, al contrario de su eterno rival. Según los datos de Opta, el Madrid es el equipo de Europa que más ocasiones claras falla, hasta 25, por las 18 del Dortmund o 17 del Bayern, en una lista de 10 entre los grandes del viejo continente. También es segundo el equipo que más remates a puerta cosecha, con 58, solo superado por los 0 del Barça. El Madrid necesita algo más de tres remates para hacer un gol mientras que los culés algo menos de dos. Un 32,76% de los remates de los de Mou acaban en gol, mientras que los de Flick el 55%, casi el doble. El Madrid es el segundo equipo de Europa que más marca, con 19, pero el Barça marca más también porque es más efectivo de las grandes Ligas. El Dortmund y el City han anotado menos, aunque con seis partidos por los siete del Madrid, pero los primeros necesitan 2,35 remates para marcar, por los más de tres de los blancos, y 2,83 en los bávaros, por lo que son más efectivos también. Solo fallan más que el Madrid entre los grandes el Arsenal (marca cada 3,33 remates) y el City (un gol cada 3,10 remates). El potencial ofensivo del Madrid no ofrece dudas aunque pudiera ser mucho mejor si mejorara la efectividad. Solo ha dejado su casillero a cero en la derrota ante el Betis (1-0), pero anotó dos al Espanyol, cuatro a la Real, cuatro al Málaga, cuatro al Rayo, tres al Elche y dos al Inter. Pese al juego más que mejorable en el estreno en Champions, también por culpa de las bajas en la medular, los blancos fallaron un buen puñado de ocasiones claras. Mourinho parece que tiene detectado el problema. El descenso en el juego, en el control del partido, y en consecuencia en el descenso de llegadas a puerta o de efectividad ocurren sobre todo en las segundas partes, cuando el equipo se ve ya con el partido bajo control. Lo cierto es que en los últimos cuatro encuentros, el Madrid no ha ganado en las segundas partes ninguno. Si contara solo el segundo asalto, el saldo es de tres derrotas y un empate. El Madrid que jugaba y marcaba en el primer tiempo intentó vivir de las rentas y lo pagaba caro. A nivel individual, la falta de acierto que Vinicius no ayuda a mejorar estos números. Hasta el brasileño perdió perdón en sus redes sociales tras fallar un buen número de ocasiones ante el Elche. De 6 disparos esta temporada a puerta, ha anotado solo un gol, algo más del 16% de sus remates. Mbappé mantiene su línea de la campaña pasada y un 30,7% acaban en gol. Bellingham ha recuperado el olfato con Mourinho jugando más cerca del área y un 33.3% de sus remates acaban en la red (3 de 10). Sin embargo, el jugador más efectivo es Carlos Espi, que en solo cinco remates ha hecho dos goles, un 66,6% de sus remates suben al marcador. Su tanto ante el Elche sirvió para ganar el partido, como ya ocurrió con su tanto en el minuto 90 en el primer partido de Liga frente al Espanyol. Igual le ocurre a Güler, dos goles en tres remates a puerta.

articles.title: New FSU Rumors on Jimbo Fisher Amid Mike Norvell Hot Seat, Contract Buyout Buzz
articles.summary: Sometimes you have to go backward to go forward.
articles.body:
Sometimes you have to go backward to go forward.

With Florida State off to a 1-1 start this season after going a combined 7-17 the last two years under Mike Norvell, Bruce Feldman of The Athletic reported the ACC program is "looking into the possibility" of bringing back former head coach Jimbo Fisher should it fire Norvell.

Fisher was the head coach of the Seminoles from 2010 until 2017, when he left to take over at Texas A&M.

5 Teams That Can Crash the CFB Playoff 🏈

While he struggled to establish Texas A&M as a national contender with a 45-25 record across six seasons that ended with his firing and an approximately $77 million buyout , he led Florida State to an 83-23 record and won the national championship for the 2013 campaign.

"Jimbo's rosters didn't stink," a source told Feldman. "His ability to adapt to modern football is what caught up with him."

Feldman noted Florida State "wasn't aggressive at all in the portal this offseason with a nod toward saving its money for something else down the road. That something else could be paying some of the near $50 million the school would owe Norvell if he were fired."

He also suggested Fisher may be more willing to direct some of the money that would otherwise be used to hire a new coach toward improving the roster given the size of his buyout with the Aggies.

It would be something of a shocking move, but things have also trended in the wrong direction for Florida State since Fisher left.

Willie Taggart didn't even last two full seasons while going 9-12, and Norvell has been unable to replicate the brief success he enjoyed in 2022 and 2023 when he went a combined 23-4. Since then, the Seminoles went 2-10 in 2024 and 5-7 in 2025.

They have fallen behind Miami inside their own state and face a daunting schedule with matchups against nationally ranked foes in Alabama, Virginia, Louisville and the Hurricanes all before November.

If they struggle during that stretch, they may turn back to a familiar face.

articles.title: Millwall v West Ham United: 14-year wait for derby meeting ends at The Den
articles.summary: More than 14 years after their most recent meeting, the rivalry between Millwall and West Ham United will be renewed at The Den on Saturday.
articles.body:
Millwall and West Ham United have not met in a competitive fixture since February 2012.

Since then, managers have changed, players have moved on, both clubs have experienced plenty of highs and lows, and the rivalry has been left largely to memories, stories and old footage.

The Den will host the 100th competitive meeting between the two clubs, with West Ham making the short trip.

The two clubs are separated by few miles but the significance of the fixture goes well beyond geography.

Rivalries renewed: The derby games back this season

Quiz: Can you remember West Ham & Millwall's last derby?

This is a meeting that has been passed down through generations of supporters, though for some younger fans it will be their first experience of the derby.

Millwall supporter George Cole was only 10 when the sides met most recently in 2012. He has grown up knowing the significance of the fixture without having the chance to experience it during his adult years as a supporter.

"I was very young at the time so in my prime years I've not been able to experience this fixture," he told BBC Radio London.

"It's important, from a Millwall point of view, to play the game rather than the occasion.

"There's a certain level of passion which is needed and will go into the game, but composure is also important."

While the occasion will dominate the build-up, both managers are keen to make sure their players remain focused on what happens once the noise dies down.

West Ham boss Nuno Espirito Santo knows exactly what Saturday represents.

"All of us have experienced matches like this, they are so special for the clubs," said the Portuguese manager.

"I've been involved in many rivalries in my career, many of our players also - and we know everything is inside of the pitch.

"Inside of the pitch is where things happen, what dictates the games. It's not the noise, it's not the 40,000 or the 20,000, it's inside the pitch.

"Of course, it's a special game and we're aware."

West Ham go into the game in a very different position to their hosts - they are top of the Championship having responded strongly after a disappointing opening run by putting together a sequence of positive league results.

Their most recent Championship outing was an emphatic 6-0 win over Wrexham although they were beaten 3-2 by Fulham in the Carabao Cup in midweek.

Nuno's side will now attempt to carry their league form into an atmosphere which will be unlike anything they have experienced in the division so far.

The manager says experienced players have an important role to play in helping younger members of the squad handle the emotion of the occasion.

The message from the West Ham camp is therefore not to shy away from the rivalry but to embrace it without allowing it to distract from the football.

'If you need motivation for this game, you shouldn't be playing football'

For Millwall boss Alex Neil, the challenge is rather different.

Millwall are depleted by injuries, with 14 players currently unavailable, while a run of four consecutive midweek fixtures has stretched the squad further.

Their latest test came on Tuesday at Middlesbrough, where they led 2-0 before being pegged back to draw 2-2.

Neil said afterwards that his players were "running on empty" yet there was no suggestion Saturday's game could come at a worse time.

"It means a lot to everybody - we'll give it everything," Neil said after the Middlesbrough game.

And when asked about the motivation required for a fixture of this magnitude, his answer was blunt.

"If you need motivation for this game, you shouldn't be playing football," the Scot said.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal: Barcelona star says he's experienced racism a thousand times
articles.summary: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal says he has experienced racism "a thousand times", because people are unaware their comments or behaviour are offensive.
articles.body:
Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal says he has experienced racism "a thousand times", because people are unaware their comments or behaviour are offensive.

The Spanish Observatory on Racism and Xenophobia, a government agency, said earlier this year that the 19-year-old and Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr were the most frequent targets of online racist abuse in Spain in the final quarter of 2025.

Lamine Yamal was among the Barca players targeted by racist abuse during El Clasico against Real Madrid at the Bernabeu in October 2024.

And in an interview with broadcaster Movistar, the winger, who helped Spain to win the World Cup in July, said he had encountered racism on a regular basis during his rise to prominence.

"A thousand times. People are indirectly racist toward you, but maybe don't realise it," he said.

"There are a lot of comments or looks that are racist and they don't even notice.

He added: "If someone calls me Black, it's not going to bother me at all, ultimately I'm Black, I'm not any other colour.

"Another thing is whether it's good or bad, whether they're saying it to offend me.

"But if I'm playing a match and they paid for a ticket to see me, I'm not going to get angry just because they disrespected me."

images.caption: Image caption, Lamine Yamal has won La Liga three times since making his Barcelona debut as a 15-year-old

articles.title: JJ Gabriel: Man Utd youngster travels to Barcelona amid speculation over future
articles.summary: Man Utd youngster JJ Gabriel travels to Barcelona as some of Europe's biggest clubs continue to vie for his signature.
articles.body:
Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has travelled to Barcelona as some of Europe's biggest clubs continue to vie for his signature.

The 15-year-old has told United he wants to cancel his registration with immediate effect.

BBC Sport reported on Thursday that Real Madrid have a firm interest in the forward, and Bayern Munich, Paris St-Germain and Barcelona are also known to be keen.

It is understood Gabriel left the UK on Thursday and went to France, but is now in Barcelona.

If United hold on to the Londoner's registration, it would stop him moving to another English club until the end of the season.

But if he obtains a European Union passport through either his father - a former Republic of Ireland international - or mother, who has Greek-Cypriot heritage, he could join a club in the EU when he turns 16 on 6 October.

Gabriel has not trained at United since scoring a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut on 10 September. Tournament rules prevent him from playing for a side other than United in this season's competition.

Sources close to Gabriel were furious the club did not register him for their Champions League opener with Sabah FK, which Michael Carrick's side won 4-0.

The United manager was again asked about Gabriel on Friday at his news conference to preview Sunday's Premier League match against Fulham.

"He's a young boy, JJ, and I think it's important we don't play anything out here," he said.

"With the exposure and scrutiny and everything, you got to be careful and be sensible and think of him as much as anything.

"The situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's OK is the important thing."

Gabriel scored in his first two Premier League 2 outings for United this season but will not be involved against Brentford at Leigh Sports Village on Friday.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappé leaves Nike to sign with sportswear brand On
articles.summary: Nike had sponsored the Real Madrid star since he was a child.
articles.body:
Soccer superstar Kylian Mbappé has ended his long-time relationship with Nike and signed with Swiss brand On.

The Real Madrid forward had been sponsored by Nike since he was a child, but will now join On to develop and test the brand's cleats and apparel. French soccer legend Thierry Henry will now serve as the brand's director of football after working with the company since late 2025.

"From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow's game," Mbappé said in a statement. "I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what's possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football. We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning."

Mbappé is the latest athlete to leave Nike, joining Arsenal captain Martin Ødegaard, tennis star Emma Raducanu, and Barcelona and Spain standout Lamine Yamal .

On began in 2010 making running shoes before tennis icon Roger Federer became a co-owner of the company in 2019. Its athlete lineup includes:

According to The Athletic , On's football cleats will go on sale in 2027 as "premium" products, and the company will be targeting the women's market before next summer's Women's World Cup. Mbappé is expected to debut his new cleats in the next few weeks.

articles.title: Uefa and Concacaf demand Fifa pays $10m to all 211 member countries
articles.summary: Uefa and Concacaf issue a joint statement calling on Fifa to pay $10m from its cash reserves to each of the 211 member associations.
articles.body:
Uefa and Concacaf have written to Gianni Infantino calling on Fifa to pay at least $10m (£7.5m) from its cash reserves to each of the 211 member associations.

It is the latest chapter in the war of words between the governing bodies, in response to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's aborted private equity proposal.

Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to an investment company.

The idea was scrapped after four days following widespread opposition from national associations.

The letter, seen by BBC Sport, was signed by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin and his Concacaf counterpart Victor Montagliani.

It outlines that "Fifa is on course to close 2023-26 with reserves of approximately $6bn (£4.5bn)" which is "considerably more than is required" through to the 2030 men's World Cup.

It said that Fifa should "make at least $10m available to each of its 211 member associations over the 2027-30 cycle" which should be used "for investment in infrastructure and football development".

This "one-off release of reserves" would come at a cost of $2.11bn (£1.57bn), and would be in addition to the regular funding in the cycle.

When the controversial plan was revealed in the days following the World Cup final, Infantino told members they would receive $40m (£30m) if they backed it.

Infantino set a deadline of 19 September for federations to accept his plans if they want to access an initial $20m (£15m).

In the letter, Ceferin and Montagliani said analysis carried out on Fifa's published financial statements and budgets raised doubts that the FFE proposal was "necessary to deliver greater resources".

It added that the analysis was "deliberately conservative" and a larger distribution from the reserves should be considered by the Fifa Council once the financial position at year-end is known.

An "independent review" of Fifa's finances should be commissioned, it added, with "full access to the underlying figures and assumptions".

"Fifa currently holds billions of dollars in accumulated reserves," it read. "These resources belong to football and exist to serve the game and its 211 member associations.

"Prudence should not prevent a careful examination of whether a portion could responsibly be released to the extent those reserves exceed Fifa's foreseeable needs.

"Releasing part of these reserves would demonstrate that member associations should not have to choose between development and good governance; between investment and integrity; or between financial support and the ability to consider proposals on their merits.

"Development is an institutional responsibility of Fifa – not a matter of individual discretion."

Another letter, also seen by BBC Sport, has been sent to the presidents of the other confederations - Asia, Africa, South America and Oceania - asking them to support the motion.

The news comes a day after Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt sent a letter to Infantino and Fifa secretary general Mattias Grafstrom demanding that all documents relating to the controversial FFE plan were released.

Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president, said that the Fifa Council should also receive a written explanation for the cancelled suspension of United States forward Folarin Balogun at the World Cup.

Infantino was told he should make all documents available before the next Fifa Council meeting, which is on 15 October.

Infantino, 56, will stand for election for a fourth time in March, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

images.caption: Image caption, Gianni Infantino was first elected as Fifa president in 2016

articles.title: Michele Kang says London City Lionesses' new training ground will set a new standard in women's football
articles.summary: Michele Kang believes London City Lionesses' planned new training ground will set a new standard in the women's game and surpass facilities used by most men's Premier League clubs.
articles.body:
Michele Kang believes London City Lionesses' planned training ground will set a new standard in the women's game and surpass facilities used by the majority of men's Premier League clubs.

Over the summer, Kang boosted the Women's Super League side with significant investment in players, including the signing of two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas .

Speaking to BBC Sport, Kang revealed a purpose-built training centre is expected to open within the next year.

She said: "We're building a state-of-the-art training centre for our female athletes dedicated to them, built and designed for them, which will open in less than a year.

"Our architect, who has built several Premier League training centres told me that by the time the London City training centre is up and running, it would be better than with the majority of Premier League men's teams training centres."

Kang views investment in infrastructure as part of a wider remit to ensure female athletes are no longer treated differently from their male counterparts.

"How could you possibly accept the notion that your girls, your daughters, granddaughters, sisters are treated as second-class citizens where in the same sport the boys go to play as if it's their birthright?"

She believes that for too long, women have been treated like "small men".

"We have to take care of our female players better so that they can train, perform, and thrive as female athletes, not small men," she said.

"You drive your boy to a state-of-the-art training centre and then, if you're lucky enough to have a facility nearby, you drive your girl somewhere else. Why would you accept that?"

Kang is a strong advocate of independent women's clubs and said that was one of the reasons she was attracted to London City Lionesses.

"My first entree into women's football was Washington Spirit, in the United States, where two thirds of women's teams are independent and not affiliated with men's team. So to me, that's a lot more normal.

"I wanted to show that there isn't just one model that the women's team has to be part of the men's team, but an independent team, because I think at that time, London City and Durham, if I'm not mistaken, those are the two, women-only teams.

"I wanted to build a women-only team to show when you really devote all your attention and resources and energy into women's only team, what's possible."

Kang traces much of that belief back to her upbringing in South Korea and the influence of her father.

When asked why she is so passionate about women, Kang said: "I think it probably originally came from my father. From very early on, my father, who had only three girls. It maybe was a necessity.

"I was growing up in South Korea, where it was still a very traditional society, where girls have certain roles.

"He said in this day and age it doesn't matter whether you're a girl or a boy, whatever you want to do, you have to put 100% of what you have and you can go for it. And if you don't achieve, you have only yourself to blame."

Kang says those lessons have stayed with her throughout her career.

"I'm grateful that I achieved my American dream. And this is my way of giving back that I don't want, quite frankly, a lot of young girls growing up going through what I went through.

"I want them to be able to focus on what they have to do to be the best football player, not having to worry about changing clothes in the middle of a public park or broken equipment - all those type of things."

The club's training centre is also expected to support research into female athlete health, an area Kang believes has been overlooked for decades. Kang pointed to injury rates as one example.

"There are more ACL, injuries among female players. The tune of two or three times more female players get ACL injuries than male players," she said.

"Something like 94% of all science medical research is dedicated to men. So there's just fundamentally so little known about female body."

Kang's ambitions extend beyond London. Through her multi-club ownership model, which already spans England, France and the United States, she wants the standards being established at London City to be replicated across the globe.

"I would like to buy a team in Asia. I would like to buy a team in Africa. I would like to buy a team in South America, because I want all the girls in those countries to grow up thinking that this kind of the best, best, facilities and best practices and unbelievably, infrastructure is not something that they can only watch on TV because they're only in England, France, America, but it's in their backyard."

The owner says she wants future generations of female players to enjoy opportunities equal to those available to boys, regardless of where they grow up.

"That reality, the gap between the girls and boys journeys is indefensible, and I want that to disappear."

And when asked what message she had for the rest of the Women's Super League, her answer was short and direct.

images.caption: Image caption, Michele Kang studied at the Ewha Woman's University, a private institute in Seoul

articles.title: Celtic seek spark as Rangers aim for further derby joy
articles.summary: Early season momentum has shifted dramatically going into the first Old Firm league derby of the season on Sunday at Celtic Park.
articles.body:
Celtic and Rangers square up again in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday with the champions reeling after a 3-0 defeat to the Ibrox side in the Premier Sports Cup quarter-finals last weekend and an opening Europa League 3-1 loss to Ferencvaros.

Pressure is intensifying on Martin O'Neill's following those disappointing displays and yet Celtic have the chance to move eight points clear of their rivals.

A third loss in a row for Celtic would leave Rangers just two points adrift.

"We're ready to go, we really are," O'Neill said. "We're getting prepared for the game. It was a difficult game last Sunday and difficult last night, but we're ready to go.

"Confidence, we're far from rock-bottom. We're still in the lead in the league. If we can win this, we can extend the lead. If we don't, going into the international break, we're still going to be in front.

"It's not the thing that you would look forward to going into an international break on three successive defeats, if that's the case.

"We've got to be a bit more inventive but the crowd will be up for this. The players are capable of turning it around."

There were questions over whether recent signings fully grasped the occasion in the loss at Ibrox, with a number of new arrivals struggling to make an impact in high profile games.

"It will probably take a little bit more time, but I think anybody who experienced last Sunday, to know what it's all about, it shouldn't need many more lessons," O'Neill explained.

Leaden, stale, disheartening - where do Celtic & O'Neill go from here?

Celtic are 'little bit broken' - but is change of shape 'worth risking'?

McInnes delivers togetherness & intensity in Old Firm gobsmacker

Momentum appears to be with Rangers given their comprehensive derby victory, making it five successive wins with four clean sheets.

Manager Derek McInnes downplayed the absence of away fans as "overhyped" but acknowledged how quickly the narrative can change in the Glasgow rivalry.

"I think you're constantly aware of that at a club like Rangers," he said.

"You're only one bad result away from getting a belt in the mouth again. You've got to try and keep those to a minimum, as much as you can.

"We've worked hard to get to where we are at the minute but equally, you've got to remind yourself, it wasn't so long ago that we were in a tough spot.

"We had a big result last week and a big performance but we want to try and deliver that again on Sunday.

"I don't think we can win the game without that. Don't think that we can just turn up and everything's going to become easy for you. You've got to work for everything you get. We'll need that a bit more, to be honest [than the home performance against Celtic]."

O'Neill confirmed that they will have to assess one or two players who came off during the defeat to Ferencvaros.

Yang Hyun-Jun remains on international duty with South Korea with the manager non-committal as to whether he may adopt a change in shape to accommodate Kasper Hogh and Camilo Duran up front.

Alistair Johnston and Callum Osmand remain sidelined with injury.

Rangers may be without striker Ryan Naderi, who suffered an ankle injury in the win over Celtic after a challenge from Mika Baur. The club has contacted Scottish FA head of refereeing Willie Collum to ask why no further punishment was administered.

One unnamed player is also a doubt for the visitors, while left-back Tuur Roomens has returned to training after injury.

Celtic's 3-1 win over Rangers in May ended a six-game winless run in league Old Firm derbies (D3 L3). The Hoops have won six of their past eight home games against Rangers in the Scottish Premiership (L2)

After a 3-0 victory in the League Cup last weekend, Derek McInnes could become only the second Rangers manager to win both of his first two Old Firm derbies, after Graeme Souness in 1986

Celtic are looking to win 14+ consecutive league matches for the first time since March 2017 under Brendan Rodgers (22), a run that ended with a 1-1 home draw with Rangers.

Rangers have scored seven goals from 128 shots in the Premiership this season, a conversion rate of 5.5% - the lowest in the division.

Five of Celtic's six home league goals this season have come in the first half of matches, with their only second-half strike at Celtic Park coming from Benjamin Nygren against Dundee on matchday one.

Rangers have used more players (26) and made the joint-most starting XI changes (18) of any side in the top flight.

articles.title: Northampton Town: Investment agreed with consortium led by Alexandre Pato
articles.summary: Northampton reach agreement with a consortium including former Brazil forward Alexandre Pato over a "proposed shareholding acquisition".
articles.body:
Northampton Town have confirmed they have reached agreement with a consortium including former AC Milan, Chelsea and Brazil forward Alexandre Pato over a "proposed shareholding acquisition" in the League Two club.

Sports Alpha Capital (SAC) had their proposed deal with the Cobblers approved by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) and English Football League (EFL) earlier this month.

In a statement, the club said they expected to be "in a position to confirm completion of the process" next week.

"Football club transactions always have many moving parts and often take a little longer than you would hope, but we are thrilled to be moving forward," said Northampton chairman Kelvin Thomas.

Joao Xavier, founding partner at Sports Alpha Capital, added: "We are very happy to have reached formal agreements.

"Obviously obtaining IFR and EFL approvals was a big step, but this is also a very important milestone, and we look forward to closing next week."

Sports Alpha Capital (SAC) had been in discussions about taking over Colchester United earlier this year but decided to pull out of a potential deal following initial talks.

Pato is named by SAC , external as one of its investors, along with Gemcorp Capital, a London-based independent investment management firm.

The size of SAC's proposed shareholding in the Cobblers has not been disclosed at this stage.

Pato, 37, retired from playing last year. He is best known for his five-and-a-half-year spell at AC Milan where he scored 63 goals in 150 matches and won the Serie A title in the 2010-11 season.

Pre-match, post-match and topical Cobblers content

The deal comes after a difficult year for the League Two side.

The Cobblers suffered relegation to the fourth tier last season, finishing bottom of League One.

They are currently 17th in League Two after winning for the first time this season when they beat Newport at home on 5 September.

In April, the club announced a pre-tax loss just short of £3m, with Thomas previously saying the proposed investment would make the club debt-free.

Northampton appointed Chris Hogg as their manager in May and brought in 13 players during the summer transfer window, including striker Matty Warhurst from Manchester City.

articles.summary: What are the key questions on Saturday in the final Scottish Premiership games before the international break?
articles.body:
It's the final round of Scottish Premiership games before a long international break, but who will be left brooding for three weeks and who will head there with the luxury of a confidence boost?

There are five top-flight games 24 hours before the top two in the table face off in Sunday's Old Firm derby.

Here are the key questions from Saturday's Premiership card.

Listen: Scottish Premiership weekend preview

Will managerless Hibs end dismal home run?

Hibernian go into their game against Aberdeen under a huge cloud after the sacking of David Gray.

Tuesday's dismal defeat by Kilmarnock was a drab ending to Gray's tenure as head coach and his 12-year stay at Easter Road but does not affect his legendary status given his exploits as a player.

John Potter has been placed in interim charge and must lift a group that has lost three Premiership games on the spin and hope to avoid a club record seventh successive home loss in the league, a run stretching back to last season.

Murmurs of discontent among the fanbase run beyond Gray and the hierarchy will be desperate for a performance and victory amid uncertainty over the long-term direction of the club.

Aberdeen will be in no mood to ease Hibs' recent woes.

After a similarly difficult start to the season, the Dons progressed to the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup with a penalty shootout win over Kilmarnock before thumping Motherwell 4-0 on Tuesday.

Head coach Stephen Robinson spoke about the growing confidence among his squad and it was evident at Fir Park.

Moroccan forward Ayoub Mouloua typified that with his bag of flicks and tricks, and indeed his wonderful goal, and could provide Robinson with an exciting option moving forward.

Before the Motherwell win, Aberdeen had gone four league games without a win and without a goal.

They could go as high as fourth with a win on Saturday, which would be a remarkable turnaround for Robinson and his players.

Will Kilmarnock build on first league win?

Another team whose manager and players had come under serious pressure recently is Kilmarnock, who eased some of the disquiet around Rugby Park with their 1-0 win at Easter Road.

Manager Neil McCann bristled after their first league victory of the season, insisting he maintained confidence despite taking one point from their first five outings.

More than the result, it was the performance and the clean sheet that will have heartened McCann.

Killie had shipped 14 league goals before their trip to Edinburgh, but they were much improved at the back and, in truth, should have won by a greater margin.

If they are to climb off the bottom of the table, they need to back up their midweek win with another three points against opposition from the capital.

Heart of Midlothian suffered a surprise defeat by Falkirk on Tuesday after four straight league wins - and nine overall without defeat - and head coach Wouter Vrancken was open in his disappointment in the performance level.

"It was not just out of possession we didn't play our best game, but in possession was, I think, the worst game we played," he said.

"We didn't push the opponent in decision-making and defensively then it's easy to defend and that's not how we want to play."

Indeed, two derby successes against Hibs are Hearts' only victories in their past 10 away trips in the Premiership. They lost on their last visit to Rugby Park in March and they head to Ayrshire with injuries leaving them short in defence and central midfield.

Set-pieces could be key, with third-top Hearts having scored a league-high four goals from those this season, while Kilmarnock's five goals conceded is the most in the division.

Will Motherwell get over 'bump in the road'?

Motherwell manager Alfred Johansson described the 4-0 defeat at home to Aberdeen as "a bump in the road", but with one win in seven outings, the Fir Park project is in danger of veering off course.

The Swede takes his side to Dundee having not won in five away games since defeating Hibs on the opening weekend of the Premiership season.

Johansson stressed that it is "a learning process" with "10 new players in the door", but that is hardly unique given how common such a high turnover in personnel has become in the league.

Having earned plaudits for continuing the adventurous passing style so successful for predecessor Jens Berthel Askou, he has "massive belief" that his "super committed" players will reach the great potential he sees in them.

Dens Park is the kind of venue where he will need to take points if another top-six finish is achievable and especially so when Dundee have not won in their latest two home games and three overall.

With six first-team players missing through injury or suspension, Steven Pressley is lamenting "probably one of the most challenging periods, in terms of injuries, in my time as a head coach".

So much so that 21-year-old striker Joe Westley has opted not to have surgery to repair a fractured cheekbone and trained in a protective mask.

However, considering Ryan Finnigan leads the Premiership statistics for tackles, Owen Bevan has made the most interceptions, while Ethan Hamilton has won most possession, Dundee have the ideal ingredients to disrupt Motherwell's free-flowing style and put another spanner in the works.

articles.title: El 'Pichichi' Gueye desatasca el ataque amarillo
articles.standfirst: El senegalés ya suma tres goles para ser el futbolista más efectivo del Villarreal
articles.summary: El senegalés ya suma tres goles para ser el futbolista más efectivo del Villarreal
articles.body: La versatilidad de Pape Gueye propicia que pueda colaborar en diversas funciones a la hora de ayudar a su equipo. Pero a buen seguro que al senegalés no se le carga con la responsabilidad de cargar con el peso del ataque amarillo. Pese a ello, es lo que está haciendo en este inicio de temporada, donde con tres goles se ha erigido en el máximo anotador de su equipo para paliar la falta de acierto de los arietes amarillos. Ante el Málaga el mediocentro africano tuvo un papel fundamental en la victoria castellonense al anotar dos de los tres goles de su equipo pese a salir desde el banquillo. Tantos que se unen al que anotó en la jornada inicial en el Sardinero y ante el Racing para superar los dos que ya suman Gerard Moreno o Nico Pépé: “Estoy contento porque era un partido complicado, estamos en un proceso con un nuevo entrenador. Estamos contentos después de ganar tras cinco partidos y ahora toca ganar al Levante”, afirmaba tras el duelo ante el Málaga. El ex del Marsella, que destaca por tener un buen disparo desde la larga distancia, ha colaborado con goles desde su llegada al Villarreal, donde había sumado un total de 10 en sus dos anteriores campañas . En este arranque de temporada está mostrando un enorme acierto al convertir en tres tantos sus cinco lanzamientos a puerta, uno de ellos de penalti. Precisamente, el lanzamiento desde los once metros que cerró la victoria en La Rosaleda vino precedido por cierta polémica, ya que generó una disputa con su compañero, Mikautadze, por lanzar dicha pena máxima. El georgiano se mostró contrariado al final del partido y no se quedó celebrando el triunfo con sus compañeros. El técnico amarillo, Iñigo Pérez, quiso quitar hierro al final del partido: “Sobre las órdenes de los tiradores, la emoción y el contexto que se vive dentro no se vive fuera, por tanto, para dirigir ese tipo de situaciones, muchas veces igual te falta información. He visto el típico intercambio de dos jugadores que quieren tirar el penalti para marcar. No creo que vaya a mayores; además, tienen una excelente relación los dos”.

articles.body: Roberto Fernández está viviendo el momento más importante de su carrera. El delantero del Espanyol ha irrumpido en la convocatoria de la selección española después de un espectacular inicio de temporada, con seis goles que han llamado la atención de Luis de la Fuente. Desde Puente Genil, su localidad natal, hasta Barcelona, el delantero no ha dejado de crecer. Málaga, sin embargo, sigue siendo un lugar especial para él. Allí se formó como futbolista y allí dejó uno de los mejores recuerdos recientes de la cantera blanquiazul, con más de 20 goles que resultaron decisivos para devolver al equipo al fútbol profesional. El problema es que su salida de La Rosaleda todavía genera malestar. Roberto abandonó el Málaga por apenas 1,8 millones de euros en una operación que el club no supo encauzar a tiempo. La renovación se enquistó y, cuando aparecieron equipos con mayor capacidad económica, la entidad perdió la posición de fuerza que tenía inicialmente. Tampoco llegó desde Martiricos una propuesta salarial a la altura de las nuevas circunstancias del delantero. Una situación que posteriormente ha servido de aprendizaje para la actual dirección deportiva, que ha blindado a jóvenes como Chupete o Larrubia con contratos y cláusulas acordes a su potencial. El contraste con la situación actual de Roberto es evidente. El delantero tiene una cláusula que ronda los 25 millones de euros y que podría aumentar en caso de debutar con la selección española. A ello hay que añadir los 10 millones que el Sporting de Braga obtuvo con su traspaso al Espanyol y el resto de operaciones anteriores. El valor generado por los distintos movimientos del futbolista supera ya ampliamente los 35 millones de euros. Una cifra que multiplica por casi veinte lo ingresado por el Málaga en su salida. El Braga y el Espanyol han encontrado en Roberto Fernández una operación de enorme rendimiento económico. En Málaga, mientras tanto, queda la sensación de haber dejado escapar demasiado pronto a un delantero formado en casa. El club todavía puede percibir cantidades a través del mecanismo de solidaridad de la FIFA, pero son ingresos muy alejados de los que habría generado una venta acorde con la evolución que posteriormente ha experimentado el futbolista.

articles.title: Patrick Vieira: Senegal job an 'absolute dream' for former Arsenal midfielder
articles.summary: Former France international Patrick Vieira, a World Cup winner in 1998, says taking charge of Senegal, the nation of his birth, is an "honour".
articles.body:
Patrick Vieira says it is "an honour" to become Senegal head coach, with the decision to take the job "one from the heart".

The 50-year-old was born in the West African nation but subsequently represented France as a player, winning the 1998 World Cup and the 2000 European Championship with Les Bleus.

The former Arsenal midfielder spoke of his "immense pride" to begin his first international job, following stints with New York City, Nice, Crystal Palace, Strasbourg and Genoa, at his unveiling by the Teranga Lions on Friday.

"Being head coach of the Senegal national team is an absolute dream," he told a news conference in Dakar.

"I was born here, my parents were born here, and it really is a homecoming.

"From the very first meetings I had with the [Senegal football federation] president, I accepted this challenge straight away, because there was also an exceptional generation of players.

"I realise the expectations of the people - all 20 million Senegalese. And I know that with the experience I have, with the determination I have, I'll be able to see this project through."

Taking over after the dismissal of Pape Thiaw, Vieira inherits a Senegal side which exited the 2026 World Cup in dramatic fashion in the last 32, throwing away a 2-0 lead after 85 minutes against Belgium before losing 3-2 following extra time.

Before that the Teranga Lions claimed the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) title with a 1-0 extra-time win over Morocco in January.

However, the ultimate destination of the trophy will be decided by the Court of Arbitration for Sport after a walk-off by some Senegal players and staff protesting against a penalty decision in the final resulted in the trophy being handed to the North African hosts instead in March.

"Today, Senegal is among the major nations in world football," Vieira said.

"Senegal's objectives aren't what they were 10 or 15 years ago. On the back of its recent results, Senegal has moved forward, has reached new levels.

"The demand for results has also stepped up. We need to lay solid foundations."

Vieira plans to build a side with "a very precise structure" which can play with "intensity and aggression".

"What matters to me isn't starting again from scratch," he added.

"It's about respecting what the federation has put in place over the last few years and building the next stage, opening a new chapter.

"A new chapter meaning my job isn't to tear everything down, it isn't to throw everything out of the window.

"It's about keeping this team's strength: its identity, its unity, its ability to suffer together.

"To make this project work, I'll need the whole nation united. I'll work heart and soul to restore the team's pride."

Vieira has been thrust straight into competitive action in qualifiers for the 2027 Afcon with two fixtures in this international window, two more in November and the final two rounds in March 2027.

His stint in charge was due to begin with a home match against Mozambique on Friday, 25 September but the fixture has been reversed as Dakar is in the midst of preparations for the 2026 Youth Olympic Games .

"Of course, I'd have preferred to play the first match here in Dakar but unfortunately, with the federation, we all felt the best decision was to postpone the match and go and play in Mozambique," Vieira explained.

"Those are difficulties we're going to accept and deal with."

Senegal will be without several notable names for the trip to Maputo and the subsequent away game against Ethiopia on 29 September.

Long-time number one Edouard Mendy, 34, has retired from Teranga Lions duty and Vieira said talismanic forward Sadio Mane will be absent with "a bit of a physical issue".

Despite previous speculation that Mane, also 34, could follow Mendy into retirement, Vieira said the former Liverpool and Bayern Munich man will "surely" be part of his next selection, fitness permitting.

Right-back Krepin Diatta has been left out because he is currently without a club, while forward Ismaila Sarr, who is yet to feature for Crystal Palace this season because of transfer speculation and a groin injury, is also absent.

Vieira's career as a player was trophy-laden but he has found the same kind of success hard to come by as a manager.

He departed Palace in March 2023 with a record of 22 wins from 74 games in all competitions and, after a season at Strasbourg, has been out of work since being sacked by Genoa in November last year with the Italian club bottom of the table.

He had guided them to safety in Serie A in the 2024-25 campaign but was then dismissed after six defeats in nine league games at the start of last season.

"When you talk about my coaching career, or a certain amount of experience, I've always been someone who stays positive," Vieira said.

"That means you learn, and there are always positive things to take from it. I'm a better coach today than I was in my last spell at Genoa, because that experience helped me grow and made me realise certain things.

"Given the experience I have as a manager, I've got no doubt about my ability to meet the expectations of fans."

Vieira was warmly received when he arrived in Dakar on Thursday evening, with video clips posted on social media showing him holding a Senegal flag aloft while shaking hands with a throng of fans gathered at the capital's airport.

"I couldn't have been given a warmer welcome. I saw the supporters' enthusiasm and I thank them for it.

"Taking charge of this national team isn't just a new stage in my career - it's coming back home."
